features.label_en: In late October 1822, after Isma'il demanded a heavy levy at Shendi and struck Mak Nimir, Nimir and his men burned Isma'il and his staff; the revolt spread to other regions.
The government's partiality to the Shaigiyya (and the Khatmiyya) aroused the jealousy of other groups, who then backed the Mahdi.
When Turco-Egyptian forces approached Sennar in 1821 the sultanate was too feeble to resist and capitulated.
Sultan Ibrahim was defeated and killed at Manawashi in 1874 and Darfur was annexed; Kayra family members led resistance, notably Amir Harun's revolt from 1877.

rating_basis_en.value: The Turkish administration improved irrigation and crops and gave traders greater security (p.361), but extended the Egyptian taxation system to the Sudan, which 'inevitably disrupted the economic life of the people', collected by brutal means (p.362); Muhammad Ali's gold mining at Fazughli failed (p.361).

context.control_limits_en: In 1821 the lands 'from Nubia to the Ethiopian foothills and from the Atbara to Darfur' became part of Muhammad Ali's empire (ZH_EMB_HIST2020: 从努比亚至衣索比亚山麓和从阿特巴拉河至达尔富尔). Darfur was held by the Kayra until 1874 (GHA6_CH14). In Equatoria, Baker and Gordon 'were unable to extend Turkish administration … beyond a few scattered posts' (GHA6_CH14).
context.control_limits_ar: في 1821 صارت الأراضي «من النوبة إلى سفوح الحبشة ومن نهر عطبرة إلى دارفور» جزءاً من إمبراطورية محمد علي (نص السفارة الصينية). وظلت دارفور بيد الكيرا حتى 1874 (تاريخ أفريقيا العام VI). وفي الاستوائية «عجز بيكر وغوردون عن مدّ الإدارة التركية إلى أبعد من بضع نقاط متناثرة».
